note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 or CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE write/recall run.ids.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the write
investigations.security_question: What was stored, and during which run?
investigations.learning_objective: Locate event.name=agentsec.memory.written, write run.id, memory.id, content.hash, provenance, and writer agent. An indexed memory.written row corroborates a persist event on a complete copy. It does not prove trust. It does not prove authorization.
prerequisites: a WRITE run.id from Attack Service or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id for the WRITE run. Find event.name=agentsec.memory.written. Read memory.id, content.hash, provenance. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Start with index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json and the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Paste the LIVE WRITE run.id from Attack Service, or use the Investigate write specimen REPLAY id.
investigations.hint_2: Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY uses both write and recall tokens. Write rows are event.name=agentsec.memory.written. Provenance agentsec.memory.fixture is source identity, not trust.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One write_run_id. memory.id mem.lending-preference.normal on BASELINE, mem.lending-preference.malicious on ATTACK/RETEST. Hash present. Provenance agentsec.memory.fixture.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one persist. write run.id is the writer experiment key. memory.id names the fixture. content.hash fingerprints the bytes.
investigations.security_interpretation: A complete local pack with memory.written is OBSERVED persist. Indexed rows corroborate that copy. STORED != TRUSTED. Splunk did not store the memory.
investigations.does_not_prove: Finding the write does not prove the memory was trusted, authorized, or later recalled. Empty is not SAFE.

investigations.title: Find the later recall
investigations.learning_objective: Identify agentsec.memory.recalled, current recall run.id, agentsec.memory.source_run_id, memory.id, and content.hash. Teach WRITE RUN → MEMORY → RECALL RUN. source_run_id != recall run.id.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the WRITE run.id and add the RECALL run.id. Find event.name=agentsec.memory.recalled. Confirm source_run_id equals the write run.id and is different from the current run.id.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY columns include recall_run_id and recall_source_run_id. The destination run is the later recall.
investigations.hint_2: Do not invent session.id. Correlation is memory.id + content.hash + source_run_id + current recall run.id.
investigations.expected_result_shape: recall_run_id different from write_run_id. recall_source_run_id equals write_run_id. Same memory.id.
investigations.result_explanation: Recall is a later run that loaded persisted state. Cross-run reconstruction requires both UUIDs.
investigations.security_interpretation: RECALLED != AUTHORIZED. Recalling memory is not a grant.
investigations.does_not_prove: Finding recall does not prove the memory was trusted or that a tool was authorized.

investigations.title: Verify the memory fingerprint
investigations.security_question: Did recall use the same stored content?
investigations.learning_objective: Compare memory.id, content.hash, source_run_id, and provenance across write and recall. Preview is not the authoritative content fingerprint.
investigations.starter_guidance: On Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY compare write_hash and recall_hash. Confirm provenance. Do not treat content.preview as the hash.
investigations.hint_1: content.hash is SHA-256 of the memory bytes. Preview is a bounded privacy field.
investigations.hint_2: ATTACK and RETEST should share the same malicious hash. BASELINE uses the normal hash. Matching preview text is not enough.
investigations.expected_result_shape: write_hash equals recall_hash. Same memory.id. Same provenance agentsec.memory.fixture.
investigations.result_explanation: The later recall loaded the same stored bytes. Fingerprint equality is CONTEXT evidence, not authorization.
investigations.security_interpretation: Same fingerprint proves same stored content. It does not prove trust or a grant.
investigations.does_not_prove: Matching hashes do not mean the memory is trusted. Preview equality is not the fingerprint.

investigations.title: Determine trust classification
investigations.security_question: How did CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 classify the recalled memory?
investigations.learning_objective: Find OBSERVE, memory_context_is_data, and untrusted_data. STORED != TRUSTED. OBSERVE != ALLOW.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep both run.ids. Read memory_decision, memory_reason, and recall_trust on the CONTEXT-001 row.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY columns include memory_decision, memory_reason, memory_trust_ctrl.
investigations.hint_2: Valid recalls are always OBSERVE memory_context_is_data, including ATTACK. untrusted_data is a label, not malice.
investigations.expected_result_shape: CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE, reason memory_context_is_data, trust untrusted_data on BASELINE, ATTACK, and RETEST.
investigations.result_explanation: Classification is independent of the vulnerable overlay. CONTEXT-001 does not ALLOW the tool.
investigations.security_interpretation: OBSERVE != ALLOW. The observation control did not authorize lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.does_not_prove: untrusted_data does not mean the memory is an attack. OBSERVE does not mean the content is permitted as policy.

investigations.title: Did memory influence a request?
investigations.security_question: After recall, did the agent request lookup_customer_tier at customer:read?
investigations.learning_objective: Reconstruct memory recall → request → lookup_customer_tier → customer:read. MEMORY INFLUENCE != AUTHORITY. REQUEST != GRANT.
investigations.starter_guidance: On Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY read followon_tool and followon_requested_scope. BASELINE should have no privileged follow-on. ATTACK and RETEST should request lookup_customer_tier.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt already joins CONTEXT-001 to the follow-on request fields. You are not hunting an AGENT MEMORY NOTE regex.
investigations.hint_2: ATTACK and RETEST should show the same follow-on REQUEST. That is influence, not a grant. Do not treat AGENT MEMORY NOTE as a production IOC.
investigations.expected_result_shape: BASELINE: no follow-on. ATTACK/RETEST: lookup_customer_tier / customer:read after OBSERVE.
investigations.result_explanation: The closed interpreter recognized the fixture marker and formed a request. The request is not coded_policy.
investigations.security_interpretation: MEMORY INFLUENCE != AUTHORITY. Recalled text can cause a REQUEST without becoming a GRANT.
investigations.does_not_prove: Seeing lookup_customer_tier in telemetry does not mean the tool was granted.

investigations.title: Who authorized the tool?
investigations.security_question: What did CTRL-MCP-001 decide on the follow-on request?
investigations.learning_objective: CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP. CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 did not grant the tool. The memory record did not grant the tool.
investigations.starter_guidance: Filter event.name=agentsec.control.decision on the RECALL run.id. Distinguish hop-0 CONTEXT-001 from hop-1 CTRL-MCP-001. Read decision and reason.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-AUTHZ lists control rows. Hop 0 is OBSERVE. Hop 1 is the tool PDP when a follow-on exists. Bind the recall run.id, not the write run.id.
investigations.hint_2: LIVE ATTACK hop 1: ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:memory_derived_authority. Defended RETEST hop 1: DENY tool_not_granted. Overlay reason is a lab artifact, not a production IOC.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Hop 0 OBSERVE always. ATTACK hop 1 ALLOW overlay reason. RETEST hop 1 DENY tool_not_granted.
investigations.result_explanation: The overlay is labeled lab fail-open on the recall experiment only. coded_policy still lists lookup_policy only. Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.security_interpretation: CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 did not authorize the tool. The memory record did not authorize the tool. CTRL-MCP-001 did. AcmeBank owns enforcement.
investigations.does_not_prove: ALLOW is not execution. DENY is not independently proof the handler never ran. Overlay reason is not a production IOC.

investigations.title: Did execution occur?
investigations.security_question: Is there execution evidence after the tool authorization decision?
investigations.learning_objective: ALLOW != EXECUTION. ATTACK should show mcp.started then mcp.completed and handler 1. RETEST handler = 0. Missing mcp.started is corroboration only. Runtime handler count remains authoritative.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search mcp.started / mcp.completed on the RECALL run.id. Read has_started on Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Runtime handler count remains authoritative.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-TOOL is mcp.started only. Q-MCP-EXECUTED joins control + mcp.* into execution_state. Write runs have no follow-on handler.
investigations.hint_2: LIVE ATTACK complete copy: mcp.started then mcp.completed, handler 1. Defended RETEST complete copy: zero mcp.started. Zero Splunk rows corroborate local handler count; they do not independently prove prevention. Missing mcp.started does not prove prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK: has_started=1. RETEST: no_indexed_followon_execution_event. BASELINE: no privileged start.
investigations.result_explanation: mcp.started means the handler began. mcp.completed is success of a begun call, not authorization.
investigations.security_interpretation: ALLOW != EXECUTION. Runtime lookup_customer_tier handler count is authoritative for whether the privileged operation ran.
investigations.does_not_prove: Empty Splunk is not prevention. mcp.failed after start is execution then error, not blocked.

investigations.title: Compare ATTACK vs RETEST
investigations.security_question: What stayed the same, and what changed, between the LIVE ATTACK pair and the LIVE RETEST pair?
investigations.learning_objective: SAME: memory.id, malicious content.hash, provenance, requested tool, requested scope. DIFFERENT: experiment/profile, CTRL-MCP-001 decision, execution, handler count, write/recall run.ids. SAME MEMORY. SAME REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION.
investigations.starter_guidance: Copy all four LIVE ids from Attack Service. Open the server-built ATTACK vs RETEST Search handoff. Do not paste learner SPL into Attack Service.
investigations.hint_1: Four run.ids: ATTACK write, ATTACK recall, RETEST write, RETEST recall. Fingerprints must match. If they do not, FAIL — do not rationalize.
investigations.hint_2: Do not label RETEST SAFE. One RETEST does not prove memory poisoning is solved. Splunk reconstructed the experiment. Splunk did not enforce it.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Two chains: ATTACK WRITE→RECALL→ALLOW→EXECUTE versus RETEST WRITE→RECALL→DENY→NO PRIVILEGED EXECUTION. Matching hashes.
investigations.result_explanation: The malicious bytes did not change. Server-owned ExperimentContext changed. Overlay did not persist into RETEST.
investigations.security_interpretation: SAME MEMORY. SAME REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION. Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.does_not_prove: One RETEST is not universal memory-poisoning resistance. Matching hashes do not mean SAFE.

investigations.title: What can you prove?
investigations.security_question: Which claims are SUPPORTED, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify evidence discipline. Authoritative: runtime handler count. Control evidence: CTRL-MCP-001 decision. Corroborative: complete indexed Splunk sequence. Not sufficient: DENY string, missing event, HEC acceptance, empty table, pytest.
investigations.starter_guidance: Use the PROVE tab statements. Mark each as SUPPORTED, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT against your LIVE pair plus REPLAY specimen.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED: The memory was persisted. The later recall used the same fingerprint. The memory was classified untrusted_data. CTRL-MCP-001 allowed the ATTACK request. The RETEST privileged handler did not execute.
investigations.hint_2: INCORRECT: Recalled bytes granted lookup_customer_tier. SIEM blocked the attack. Stored memory is trusted. Missing mcp.started proves prevention. One RETEST proves memory poisoning is solved. HEC HTTP 200 is searchable evidence. DENY string alone is prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: A classified list: SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT. Not a detector.
investigations.result_explanation: You reconstructed WRITE → RECALL → REQUEST → AUTHORIZATION → EXECUTION. Splunk showed a copy. Splunk did not enforce.
investigations.security_interpretation: SPLUNK != ENFORCEMENT. One successful RETEST is not universal memory-poisoning resistance.
investigations.does_not_prove: Empty tables, HEC success, overlay reason strings, and DET-MCP-001 silence do not prove SAFE.
